physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the pituitary, a gland the size of a pea hung at the base of the brain, just behind the place between the brows where the older books always pointed. It is small and central and quiet, and it speaks to almost every other gland in the body. When it speaks, the rest of the chemistry listens. It is fitting that the code of opinion and far-sightedness sits here, in the organ the body uses to coordinate the parts into one whole.

The shadow has its bodily floor in this place. When a position is being defended, when the mind is hard around its corner, there is a pressure behind the eyes and a low tightness in the forehead, the head working harder than it needs to. People rub that spot without knowing why. The body is the first to feel the cost of holding a view that has to be guarded.

When the grip lets go, that same region softens. The eyes loosen. There is a kind of seeing that begins lower than the eyes, that uses the whole face, that runs down into the chest. People speak of the third eye and place it here. It is closer to the truth to say the whole body starts taking part in the looking. The pituitary is only the small switch through which that wider seeing first comes online.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the gland, this code answers to a single amino acid, Arginine. Arginine is the body's main source of nitric oxide, the tiny signal molecule that cells use to speak to each other across the spaces between them. It tells blood vessels to open, it carries word from one cell to the next, it is the body's language of opening and signal.

There is a teaching in that, and it is the body saying the same thing the card has been saying all along. The code that gets stuck in opinion, in the hard verdict, in the closed corner, runs on the chemistry of opening. Of message passed from one cell to another without insistence. Arginine does not argue. It signals. It loosens what was clenched. The far-sightedness the card moves toward is not just a mental skill. It is the body letting one cell finally hear another, the way it was always built to.
